project_title: Job Market Analysis: Understanding Employment Trends and Recruitment Patterns Using Naukri.com Job Listings
problem_statement: Describe patterns in historical job listings, including industry, role, location, skills, experience requirements and advertised pay.
objectives: Profile the supplied job-listing sample and its data quality.
Identify listing patterns by industry, role, location, experience and extracted skill mentions.
Summarize comparable advertised salary information and its missingness.
Test selected associations and group differences using suitable statistical methods.
Create business KPIs, exploratory monthly trends and an explicitly limited three-month forecast.
Communicate findings through reproducible outputs and a three-page Power BI dashboard.
scope: Historical job advertisements in the supplied Naukri.com sample. It does not represent all vacancies, applicants, employers or the current labour market.
success_criteria: All input fields and transformations are documented.
Cleaning and validation reports are exported.
EDA, statistical results and KPIs are reproducible from the supplied CSV.
Forecasting uses chronological validation and reports MAE/RMSE.
Dashboard tables and charts can be traced to exported CSV outputs.
Limitations, bias, fairness and privacy safeguards are documented.
data_source: Naukri.com job-listings dataset supplied for academic coursework; exact collection provenance must be verified.
collection_method: Not independently verified by this script. Replace this description with the actual provenance/collection method of the supplied dataset; do not claim scraping if it was not performed.
coverage: The script computes the actual row count and posting-date coverage from the input file. The known working sample in prior analysis was approximately 22,000 listings dated 2015-2017, but verify against this run.
key_limitations: One job portal and historical sample; sampling and representation bias.
Uneven month coverage; absent months are treated as unknown, not zero.
Salary currency is not documented; values are kept as source numeric units without currency labels.
Salary statistics use only strict comparable numeric salary strings.
Skill extraction is a fixed-vocabulary keyword scan of job descriptions.
Role families and primary city are heuristic classifications.
Number of positions is missing for many listings and is not equivalent to job-post count.
Forecast is exploratory and describes sample listing counts, not current hiring demand.
ethics_and_fairness: Use only for the stated academic purpose and restrict access to raw data.
Do not attempt to identify individuals or infer protected characteristics.
Do not use these aggregate historical patterns to rank applicants or automate hiring decisions.
Check representation and missingness before comparing groups.
Keep human review and transparent documentation for any downstream recruitment use.
